# Title:Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
In this paper we propose CaMeL, a robust defense that creates a protective system layer around the LLM, securing it even when underlying models are susceptible to attacks. To operate, CaMeL explicitly extracts the control and data flows from the (trusted) query; therefore, the untrusted data retrieved by the LLM can never impact the program flow. To further improve security, CaMeL uses a notion of a capability to prevent the exfiltration of private data over unauthorized data flows by enforcing security policies when tools are called.

# [Simon Willison’s Weblog](https://simonwillison.net/)
## CaMeL offers a promising new direction for mitigating prompt injection attacks
The new paper **[Defeating Prompt Injections by Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18813)** from Google DeepMind _finally_ bucks that trend.

I called it “prompt injection” because it’s the same anti-pattern as [SQL injection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQL_injection).

It works by taking a command from a user, converting that into a sequence of steps in a Python-like programming language, then checking the inputs and outputs of each step to make absolutely sure the data involved is only being passed on to the right places.

#### Addressing a flaw in my Dual-LLM pattern [#](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Apr/11/camel/#addressing-a-flaw-in-my-dual-llm-pattern)
The Privileged LLM is tasked with planning the sequence of actions needed to fulfill the user’s request, such as searching the cloud storage for the meeting notes and fetching the requested document from the cloud storage, and sending it to the client.

#### Fixing that with capabilities and a custom interpreter [#](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Apr/11/camel/#fixing-that-with-capabilities-and-a-custom-interpreter)
In CaMeL, the user’s prompt is converted by the P-LLM into a sequence of steps that are described using code.

#### The best part is it doesn’t use more AI [#](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Apr/11/camel/#the-best-part-is-it-doesn-t-use-more-ai)
CaMeL is a practical defense to prompt injection achieving security not through model training techniques but through principled system design around language models.

#### So, are prompt injections solved now? [#](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Apr/11/camel/#so-are-prompt-injections-solved-now-)
My hope is that there’s a version of this which combines robustly selected defaults with a clear user interface design that can finally make the dreams of general purpose digital assistants a secure reality.
